\begin{abstract}
\raggedright
\code{scientific-data-analysis} v2.5 continues v2.4. v2.4 stabilized the mother
skill; v2.5 extends that work across \code{scientific-data-analysis},
\code{scientific-data-astro}, \code{scientific-data-documents},
\code{scientific-data-notebooks}, and \code{scientific-data-maintainer}.
It defers heavy content without deleting capabilities or undertaking a large
rewrite. Public scripts remain stable entrypoints; substantial executable
bodies live in \code{fixtures/}, and internal helpers in
\code{fixtures/_internal/}. The mother's substantial historical content
becomes compact stubs or external maintenance archives. Its duplicate registry
becomes a stub resolving the canonical maintainer registry.

The intended result is that the skills remain substantial domain tools,
while \code{evaluate-skill} rates them A/95 and \code{improve-skill} finds no
required fixes. A documented static warning about deferred cost remains
accepted. Scientific Workbench is not modified.
\end{abstract}
\tableofcontents

\section{Executive overview}
v2.5 changes internal architecture, not capabilities. It aims to let the
scientific-data family grow with less pressure on the context budget, without
turning each child into another oversized skill.

The conservative product decisions are:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \code{scientific-data-analysis} remains the normal public entrypoint.
\item \code{scientific-data-astro} remains the expert child for FITS, WCS, photometry, spectra, RV, and optional or legacy astronomy routes.
\item \code{scientific-data-maintainer} remains maintainer-only.
\item Public scripts remain in \code{scripts/}.
\item Substantial implementation bodies move to \code{fixtures/}.
\item Substantial internal helpers move to \code{fixtures/_internal/}.
\item The \code{public_surface_registry.yaml} public contract is preserved.
\item Scientific Workbench is not modified.
\item The canonical 61-row registry lives in maintainer; the mother keeps a compact stub resolving it for the gates.
\end{itemize}

The original guide both says that the registry is unchanged and describes
replacing the mother's duplicate with a stub. These statements refer to the
preserved public contract and the changed storage/resolution layout,
respectively.

\section{What remains unchanged}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item No new capability or public path removal.
\item No changes to scientific contracts, artifact types, errors, statuses, or app hints.
\item No forced general-purpose analogy for astronomy or legacy routes.
\item No edits to original user data.
\item No synchronization or development of Scientific Workbench.
\end{itemize}

\section{v2.5 architecture}
The pattern is:
\begin{lstlisting}[style=promptstyle]
scripts/inspect_fits.py      # stable entrypoint
fixtures/inspect_fits.py     # substantial executable body
scripts/_internal/fixture_script_dispatch.py
scripts/_internal/provenance_utils.py      # compact shim
fixtures/_internal/provenance_utils.py     # substantial internal body
scripts/_internal/deferred_internal.py     # internal loader
\end{lstlisting}
Users and gates continue to call \code{scripts/*.py}. Implementation changes
belong in the corresponding fixture. This reduces routine reading cost while
preserving historical compatibility.

\subsection{Shim rule}
Some scripts re-export a tool from another child and have no local
implementation. In astro:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \code{latex_workbench.py} continues to delegate to \code{scientific-data-documents}.
\item \code{notebook_workbench.py} continues to delegate to \code{scientific-data-notebooks}.
\end{itemize}
Converting those shims into fixture wrappers would be incorrect. v2.5 retains
them as shims and verifies that behavior through regression checks.

\newpage
\section{Plugin-eval evidence}
The important v2.5 result is closure of mandatory work and visible code
recommendations across all five skills. The final recorded installed
measurement, after compacting mother and maintainer with margin, was:
\begin{longtable}{p{0.43\linewidth}rrr}
\toprule
\textbf{Installed skill} & \textbf{Score} & \textbf{Grade} & \textbf{Deferred} \\
\midrule
\code{scientific-data-analysis} & 95 & A & 44913 \\
\code{scientific-data-astro} & 95 & A & 49754 \\
\code{scientific-data-documents} & 95 & A & 28155 \\
\code{scientific-data-notebooks} & 95 & A & 28040 \\
\code{scientific-data-maintainer} & 95 & A & 46230 \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
All five retained the \emph{deferred cost} warning.

All five \code{deferred_cost_tokens} measurements remain in the heavy band.
The original release accepts this because actual domain implementations,
wrappers, contracts, and maintenance evidence remain available. Mandatory
fixes and warnings about complexity, long lines, and long functions were
closed. Remaining backlog:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item The static \code{deferred_cost_tokens-budget-high} warning.
\item Formal coverage, if coverage metrics are desired later.
\end{itemize}

\section{v2.5 regressions}
Main regression:
\begin{lstlisting}[style=promptstyle]
python scripts/audit_v2_5_budget_deferral_regression.py
\end{lstlisting}
It validates:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item Representative astro wrappers and fixtures.
\item Astro shims that must remain shims.
\item Representative documents, notebooks, and maintainer wrappers.
\item Internal helpers deferred to \code{fixtures/_internal/}.
\item Mother maintenance wrappers.
\item The active historical matrix as a compact stub and its complete canonical fixture archive.
\item Compact historical maintainer references with archived canonical bodies.
\item A compact mother router module map that remains loadable at runtime.
\item The compact maintainer module-map copy and its archived canonical body.
\item Compact mother historical contracts/plans and their archived canonical bodies.
\item The mother's duplicate registry replaced by a canonical stub to maintainer.
\item Compact, synchronized README, RELEASE, and public snapshot documents.
\item Mother wrappers preserving their own private helpers.
\end{itemize}
Earlier gates remain in place:
\begin{lstlisting}[style=promptstyle]
python scripts/audit_v2_4_budget_architecture_regression.py
python scripts/audit_v2_3_release_candidate_regression.py
python scripts/audit_v2_3_module_ownership_regression.py
\end{lstlisting}

\section{Historical closure criteria}
The original v2.5 closure required:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.7em]
\item \code{guia_scientific_data_analysis_v2_5.tex} compiles to PDF.
\item The PDF and TeX are copied to the Desktop for that historical local handoff.
\item \code{audit_v2_5_budget_deferral_regression.py} passes.
\item Affected v2.3/v2.4 regressions pass.
\item Documents/notebooks wrapper and internal-helper smoke checks pass.
\item \code{sync_public_surface_docs.py --check} passes.
\item The editable skill is synchronized to the installed family only after green gates.
\item Post-synchronization gates pass.
\item \code{evaluate-skill} and \code{improve-skill} run on installed mother and children.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Recommended usage after v2.5}
Ordinary usage remains unchanged:
\begin{lstlisting}[style=promptstyle]
python scripts/scientific_workflow_router.py plan input --task "..."
python scripts/profile_table.py data.csv --summary-json summary.json
python scripts/inspect_fits.py image.fits --summary-json summary.json
\end{lstlisting}
For maintenance, release work, and plugin-eval:
\begin{lstlisting}[style=promptstyle]
python scripts/audit_v2_5_budget_deferral_regression.py
python scripts/audit_v2_4_budget_architecture_regression.py
python scripts/sync_public_surface_docs.py --check
\end{lstlisting}

\section{Conclusion}
v2.5 is an internal improvement rather than a visible user feature. The
modular architecture now defers substantial execution bodies, internal
helpers, and historical material as well as separating responsibilities.
It is intended to support growth while preserving compatibility and reducing
pressure on usage budgets. The original guide's aspiration about weekly usage
limits is not a measured account-level saving; its evidence is the static
plugin-eval result documented above.
